To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the amount of retained nicotine in the respiratory tract is highly dependent upon the depth of inhalation; 2) at steady state, the urinary excretion of the nicotine metabolites reflects approximately 90 % of the nicotine dose retained from smoking.
the amount of nicotine retained from cigarette smoking was approximately 100% in normal smokers and 11% in smokers who did not inhale.
most of the inhaled nicotine is retained in the respiratory tracts of smokers, and the daily urine NE excretions reflects approximately 90-95% of the retained amount of nicotine from smoking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the amount of inhaled nicotine and urinary excreted nicotine equivalents in smokers.
the development of a biomarker for the assessment of nicotine exposure in cigarette smokers.
the relationship between the amount of nicotine retained and the urinary excretion of the nicotine biomarker NE in adult male smokers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
urinary excretion of total NE is an appropriate biomarker of nicotine exposure in adult male smokers.
urinary NE is a good indicator of the amount of nicotine delivered to the lung, and that urinary NE excretion reflects the amount of nicotine retained and absorbed from cigarette smoking.

the urinary excretion of the five major nicotine metabolites (cotinine, cotinine glucuronide, nicotine glucuronide, trans 3'-hydroxylcotinine, and trans 3'- hydroxylcotinine glucuronide), expressed collectively as nicotine equivalents (as nicotine equivalents), is a good biomarker for the amount of nicotine retained from cigarette smoking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nicotine equivalents in urine reflects the total nicotine exposure from smoking.
nicotine retention from smoking is highly dependent on the smoking pattern, but at steady state, urinary excretion of the nicotine metabolites is a good biomarker of smoking exposure.
the amount of nicotine retained from smoking was highly dependent upon the smoking pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
urinary excretion of total nicotine and its five metabolites is a good biomarker for assessing the amount of inhaled nicotine and thus the amount of nicotine retained from smoking.
urinary NE is a good biomarker for estimating nicotine exposure from smoking.
the urinary excretion of the sum of nicotine and its metabolites is a good biomarker for nicotine exposure from cigarette smoking.
